pairs.subject: reference-parity-gating
pairs.evidence: src/lib/visual-gen/reference-conformance.ts:224 The reference conformance gate evaluates generated meshes against reference images through an uncalibrated single-view vision critique that lacks dual-anchor constraints, invariant registration, or real-unit work order findings.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/visual-gen/reference-conformance.ts:246 The gate compares only the reference image and rendered view via a single vision prompt, lacking an independent specification anchor that constrains scale or dimensions.

src/lib/visual-gen/reference-conformance.ts:83 Rather than establishing a coordinate frame from an invariant region, the comparison relies on unaligned images and instructs the model that camera distance, framing, and lens differ.

src/lib/visual-gen/reference-conformance.ts:93 The comparison payload emits unstructured comma-separated textual descriptions rather than located, signed deviations in real units directing automated correction.

src/lib/visual-gen/reference-conformance.ts:22 The gate acknowledges that invented non-front sides are entirely unreferenced and unmeasured, but maintains no structured blindness register assigning distinct witnesses to these blind views.

src/lib/visual-gen/reference-conformance.ts:127 Parity scoring collapses into a discrete 0-3 severity clamp rather than a weighted sum of constituent terms including high percentiles and symmetric coverage.

src/lib/visual-gen/reference-conformance.ts:84 The prompt instructs the model to ignore stylised reference presentation without any mechanism for bounding defect reach to specific rows or repairing references.

pairs.registryProposal: The standard assumes geometric comparison rigs with numeric deviation bands (e.g. cross-sections, silhouettes, vertex measurements), and could clarify how reference parity principles map onto multimodal vision model evaluation where continuous coordinate registration and real-unit delta reporting are unavailable.
